title: Mossbell — EEOC and MDHR charges
forum: EEOC Minneapolis Area Office and Minnesota Department of Human Rights; parallel charge preparation

timeline.event: Employer communicated its final promotion denial; client alleges sex discrimination
Client obtained the promotion scoring sheet
Potential witness described a different explanation given to the selected applicant
Client asked counsel to prepare both federal and Minnesota charges
Client workplan signed; draft delivery agreed for ten days after reset

documents.title: Promotion denial and scoring sheet
documents.body: SYNTHETIC DEMO DOCUMENT. The final promotion denial was communicated two hundred eighty-two days before reset; this communication is the alleged discriminatory act and the limitations trigger. Nora alleges sex discrimination. The federal scenario assumes qualifying state/local proceedings for the 300-day window; no earlier notice, tolling, or special deadline applies. No administrative charge has yet been filed.

documents.title: Witness interview summary
documents.body: SYNTHETIC DEMO DOCUMENT. Tessa Alderwick recalls that the selection panel called the night shift a poor fit for Nora, despite the highest test score. This allegation requires investigation and is not a finding. The Minnesota claim concerns the same denial; no tolling is assumed.

documents.title: Agreed workplan
documents.body: SYNTHETIC DEMO DOCUMENT. Workplan § 5: Counsel will deliver the EEOC and Minnesota charge drafts to the client. Delivery is due ten calendar days after the demo reset date. This is an agreed draft-delivery milestone, separate from any filing deadline.

deadlines.label: File EEOC charge within assumed 300-day window
Agreed delivery of parallel charge drafts

clientFacing.status: We are preparing two possible discrimination charges about the same promotion decision. No charge has been filed yet.
nextSteps: Check the promotion-denial notice and scoring sheet for accuracy.
Review both charge drafts promptly; the federal filing window closes first.
